prompt:
Convert the contact block in the incoming note into a single JSON object. The object must contain exactly name, phone, email, company, and country. All five values must be strings or JSON null. Emit the object alone, with no fences or commentary.

Read the block, not the surrounding note. It consists of labeled values with variable labels and separators (including colon, equals, and tab). Trim each value and compress internal whitespace to single spaces. A blank, absent, or placeholder value is missing. The placeholders, ignoring case, are -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, and TBD. Do not repair missing data from the narrative, signature, domain, company suffix, or any other clue. The only fallback is the international calling code rule below.

Find the source for each field. The country label always supplies the explicit country. From the other lines, pick email by the presence of @ and phone by its shape, irrespective of their labels. The phone shape is at least seven digits, with only digits, spaces, and + - ( ) . / remaining after removing a leading tel: and an extension. Extensions are trailing digits introduced by ext., ext, x, #, or extension. Use name and company labels for those fields unless the name value ends with a legal suffix and the company value does not; then exchange them. The legal suffix list is AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Match at the end, without regard to case, allowing a comma before the suffix.

Render text fields from their selected values:
- Name: if there is a comma, split at the first one and put the portion after it first. Remove leading honorifics Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, and Prof, with or without a dot, in any case. Uppercase the initial character and lowercase the remainder of each part separated by spaces or hyphens.
- Company: strip the trailing legal suffix and its optional preceding comma. Trim, then uppercase the initial character and lowercase the remainder of each space-separated word.
- Email: remove surrounding angle brackets and the leading mailto: wrapper, in the order they occur. Lowercase the entire address. Do not reconstruct it from a name or domain pattern: retain each character except for these specified transformations.
Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics in all fields. Do not transliterate.

Resolve the country and phone:
- Map a present country value to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Recognize English, Swedish, and German names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes, and common aliases, irrespective of case. UK and Great Britain map to GB; Holland to NL; USA and U.S.A. to US; Türkiye to TR; Czech Republic to CZ.
- Strip tel: and any extension from the phone. Ignoring an opening parenthesis, classify + and 00 prefixes as international. For an international number, convert 00 to +, drop (0), and strip spaces, dashes, dots, slashes, and parentheses. Preserve its calling code even if the country line disagrees.
- International phone, country present: output the normalized country line and the normalized international phone independently.
- International phone, country missing: output the normalized phone and use its calling code to fill country if that code belongs to exactly one country. If shared, as with +1 or +7, leave country null.
- National phone, country present: strip formatting and one leading trunk 0, then prepend + and that country’s calling code. National phone, country missing: phone is null as well.
- Missing phone: phone is null. Keep the normalized country line or null if missing.

Every non-null phone is E.164: + followed by the calling code and national significant number, with no punctuation or spaces after +. All other missing fields remain null.
